lines: Taylor Nguyen
+1 (555) 010-6642 | taylor.nguyen@example.com | example.com/code/tnguyen
EDUCATION
Westfield State University | M.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Westfield State University | B.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - Jun 2023
EXPERIENCE
Westfield State University | Web Developer, IT Services | Metro City, USA | Jul 2023 - Aug 2024
- Owned the department websites and the shared component library other developers relied on.
- Interviewed 8 department editors about publishing; the findings led to a preview mode that cut broken pages reported by students from 30 to 6 a month.
- Wrote the accessibility checklist for all university web pages, reducing failed audits from 12 to 2 a semester.
- Rebuilt the course-catalog search with client-side filtering, cutting search time from 4 seconds to under 1.
Lumen Travel | Frontend Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Sep 2025
- Improved page performance by 35% by code-splitting the calendar and map widgets.
- Added keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels to the date picker, fixing all 14 accessibility issues flagged in the audit.
- Wrote 60 component tests for the search filters, which caught 3 regressions before release.
- Cut the landing page's largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.2s by adding loading="lazy" to the hero image.
- Prevented cross-site scripting in comments by storing user input in React state before rendering it with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
- Rebuilt the hotel search results page in React with server-side rendering, cutting median load time from 3.8s to 1.6s and raising bookings per search 9% in an A/B test.
PROJECTS
Transit Arrival Web App | Independent Project | TypeScript, React | Oct 2025 - Present
- Built a progressive web app showing live bus arrivals for 400 stops, used by about 900 riders a week.
- Cached the stop list offline, so the app opened in 0.8s on a slow 3G connection against 2.9s before.
- Open-sourced the app, and the city transit agency linked it from its developer page.
Library Room Booking | Hackathon, Team of 4 | Vue | Feb 2024 - Mar 2024
- Worked on the frontend of the booking flow using React and TypeScript.
- Wrote the booking calendar component and its tests, handling overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.
- Rebuilt a travel search page with server rendering, more than halving its load time and lifting bookings by about a tenth.
SKILLS
Tools: TypeScript, React, Vue, Storybok, Angular
Methods: server-side rendering, accessibility, component testing

items.says: The Experience entries are not ordered newest-first.
items.because: The Westfield State University role appears above the more recent Lumen Travel internship, so a scanning reader could miss the newer frontend work.

items.says: The ownership statement does not identify a specific change you made.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether you developed the sites or mainly maintained them.

items.says: The ownership statement does not say what improved for editors, visitors, or developers.
items.because: Without an observable improvement, a reader cannot judge the effect of the work.

items.says: The preview-mode result is buried, and your role in creating the mode is unclear.
items.because: “The findings led to” does not say whether you built the mode or only supplied research.

items.says: The accessibility checklist does not say what it checked or how it was used.
The search-time figure does not identify what interval was measured.
items.because: It could mean query response time or the time a person took to find a course.

items.says: The 35% page-performance improvement does not name the metric that changed.
items.because: “Page performance” could refer to several measurements.

items.says: The sentence repeats “by” in quick succession.
Attributing the LCP drop to lazy-loading the hero image is wrong if it was the visible LCP element.
items.because: Lazy-loading a visible LCP image ordinarily delays its request and worsens largest contentful paint.

items.says: Storing input in React state does not prevent cross-site scripting when it is rendered with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
items.because: React state does not sanitize input, and dangerouslySetInnerHTML can insert attacker-controlled HTML.

items.says: The XSS-prevention claim gives no evidence that prevention was verified.
items.because: Without a test or review, “Prevented” overstates what the line establishes.

items.says: The strongest internship result is not the opening bullet.
items.because: Leading with the measured load-time reduction and A/B-tested bookings lift would make that result visible on a scan.

items.says: The live-arrivals description does not say how arrival data reaches the app.
The comparison “against 2.9s before” is awkward.
The bullet names React and TypeScript while the project heading names Vue.
items.because: The mismatch leaves readers unsure which framework belongs to the project and makes its technical description less credible.

items.says: “Worked on the frontend” does not identify the specific part you built or changed.
items.because: A reader cannot distinguish a built feature from general participation or assess your individual contribution.

items.says: The booking-flow bullet does not say what the work achieved.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether the flow became usable, more reliable, or remained in progress.

items.says: The calendar component is not the opening bullet.
items.because: It gives a clearer account of your contribution than the broad booking-flow opening.

items.says: The calendar bullet does not describe how it handled overlapping bookings or time-zone changes.
The travel-search result is wrongly presented as library-room-booking hackathon work.
items.because: The later Lumen Travel internship reports a closely matching server-rendered search result and bookings lift.

items.says: “Storybok” in Tools is misspelled.
items.because: The typo creates an avoidable accuracy concern in the skills section.
